summary: Connect counting to quantity: each next number name means one more object.
Notice that adding numbers in either order gives the same total (commutative property).
Describe coins and know their names.
Talk about time in days, months, years and seasons.
Describe where objects are relative to each other (above, beside, behind); naming shapes is left out.
Break apart and recombine numbers flexibly to add and subtract.
Add and subtract within 10 flexibly, accurately and efficiently.
Use several strategies to add and subtract within 20.
Subtract a multiple of 10 from any two-digit number.
Know the value of each coin.
Tell defining attributes of shapes from non-defining ones like color or size.
Build and draw shapes that have given defining attributes.
Add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies; no explicit from-memory goal for one-digit sums.
Skip-count by 5s, 10s and 100s.
Count, read, write and represent numbers up to 1000.
Collect measurement data and show it in several ways, not only a line plot.
Organize, show and interpret data with up to four categories.
Solve addition and subtraction problems of all types using data shown in a graph or table.
Measure and estimate liquid volume and mass in customary and metric units; solve one-step problems.
Find factor pairs and primes to 100; test whether numbers up to 1000 are multiples of a one-digit number.

state_code: # - 2026 Montana Mathematics Content Standards (OPI, "Adopted 2025, Implemented 2026"; effective July 1, 2026), K-5 on pp. 35-49:
# - Rule text, ARM 10.53.502-10.53.507 "[Effective 7/1/2026] ... version 2" (checked K-5 wording and item counts; they match the OPI document):
# - OPI writes MT.<grade>.<domain>.<number>, e.g. MT.K.CC.1, MT.3.NF.2 (no cluster letters; sub-bullets are not coded). Used here as state_code.
# - The ARM rule numbers the same items by grade rule and letter: ARM 10.53.502 = K, .503 = grade 1 ... .507 = grade 5;
#   e.g. MT.K.CC.1 = ARM 10.53.502(1)(a), MT.K.OA.6 = 10.53.502(2)(f). Domain/letter order matches the MT code numbering.
# - Numbering diverges from CCSS where Montana added or split standards: grade 1 OA 7-9, MD 4-5, G 2-4; K OA.6, MD.4-5; grade 2 MD.11.
# - None entirely. Partly dropped or narrowed:
#   K.CC.B.4a/4b (one-to-one counting, last number = count) not stated; K.G.A.1 naming shapes in the environment not stated;
#   1.OA.B.3 properties as strategies replaced by compose/decompose (commutativity moved to K.OA.6; associativity not stated);
#   2.OA.B.2 "know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers" not stated; 2.MD.D.9 line plot not required (any display).
# - Many standards are shortened restatements that drop CCSS examples, limits and sub-parts (e.g. 2.OA.C.4 5x5 limit, 4.MD.A.1 unit list); marked "same".
# - K: commutative property (K.OA.6), coin names (K.MD.4), days/months/years/seasons (K.MD.5).
# - Grade 1: coin values (1.MD.4); subtract multiples of 10 from any two-digit number (1.NBT.6).
# - Grade 3: customary units for liquid volume and mass (3.MD.2). Grade 4: multiples test up to 1000 (4.OA.4).
# - Many standards add "should incorporate cultural context relating to Montana Indigenous Peoples and local communities" (Indian Education for All);
#   this is a context requirement, not math content, and did not change "kind".
# - Official Appendix A errors/differences: MT.K.CC.4 is listed as "CCSS.K.CC.B.1 and K.CC.B.1.c" (no such codes; K.CC.B.4/4c meant);
#   MT.3.MD.8 listed as 3.MD.C.8 (real code 3.MD.D.8); grade 4 MD/G and grade 5 NF/MD/G codes are missing cluster letters or grade numbers.
# - Appendix A says MT.1.G.2 (build/draw shapes with defining attributes) and MT.2.MD.11 (solve problems from data) have no CCSS match;
#   their content is the second half of 1.G.A.1 and 2.MD.D.10, so they are mapped there.
# - K.OA.6 marked "moved" from 1.OA.B.3; K.MD.4 and 1.MD.4 (coins) marked "moved" from 2.MD.C.8 (CCSS never states coin identification); Appendix A says "no corresponding standard" for all three.
# - MT.2.NBT.3 also given 2.NBT.A.2 because "count within 1000" moved out of MT.2.NBT.2 into it.
# - kind is judged on content against CCSS 2010; Montana's shortened wording often omits CCSS examples and number limits.
